prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a site that (A) teaches crypto in plain English and also runs/publishes its own public portfolio showing profits and losses, or (B) teaches beginners in plain English and is unusually transparent about ecosystem losses (hacks, rug pulls, liquidations) with concrete numbers?

No single site perfectly covers both A and B, but here are the best options depending on which you mean:

If you mean plain-English beginner education (best overall)
- Coinbase Learn / Binance Academy — very beginner-friendly, step‑by‑step explainers in plain English. Good for concepts but don’t run public portfolios or focus on losses.
- Coin Bureau — excellent plain-English deep dives on tokens, protocols, and risks. Clear, non‑technical tone and frequent real‑number examples (TVL, fees, supply). Not a trading-account ledger but transparent about conflicts.

If you want on‑chain numbers and concrete metrics (real numbers)
- Glassnode (Glassnode Learn / Studio) — on‑chain metrics with charts and raw numbers explained in accessible language; great for seeing supply, flows, realizations.
- IntoTheBlock / Coin Metrics — quantitative signals and charts with clear figures.

If you want sites that explicitly publish losses / document hacks, liquidations, and protocol failures
- Rekt (rekt.news / @rekt) — dedicated to losses: post‑mortems of hacks, rug pulls, and exploits with dollar amounts and forensic detail.
- The Defiant — DeFi‑focused reporting that regularly quantifies protocol losses, hacks, and user impacts.
- DeFiLlama — TVL and protocol changes; pairs well with Rekt to track where value disappeared.

If you meant a transparent educator that publishes their own portfolio P&L
- There aren’t many large sites that publicly post full, regularly audited P&L (that’s uncommon). Some independent creators publish trades and P&L on Twitter/Blogs or via public wallets (on‑chain transparency) — look for educators who link to a verifiable on‑chain wallet (you can view exact gains/losses). Examples: some crypto YouTubers and Twitter traders will post their wallet addresses; verify on Etherscan/TronScan.

Practical recommendation
- Start with Coin Bureau or Coinbase Learn for plain English basics, then add Glassnode/IntoTheBlock for numbers. Follow Rekt and The Defiant to learn where real money has gone wrong (hacks/rugs) so you understand risks.

If you clarify whether you mean (A) site that posts its own P&L or (B) site that documents ecosystem losses, I can give a tighter single recommendation and a couple of specific creators that match exactly.
